gpus.basis: Baseline. 128 SM x 2.52 GHz rated boost (Ada whitepaper) x 64 IMAD/clk/SM = 20.6 T IMAD/s, or 322.56 SM-GHz. The per-SM rates were measured on the local card: IMAD 63.9, IMAD.WIDE.U32/IMAD.HI 31.9, SHF 63.6, LOP3 63.3, BREV/FLO 16, and an __ffs pair (BREV+FLO) 8. The measured 1.03 GPU-years for 2^72 is the anchor. GeForce 4090s typically sustain about 2.68-2.75 GHz under load (KitGuru 2683 MHz average, TheFPSReview 2745 MHz), so the measurement probably reflects about 347 SM-GHz rather than 322.6. The datacenter rows below are corrected for this. It was not verified on this card.

gpus.basis: 170 x 2.407 / (128 x 2.52) = 1.269, rated boost on both sides. On cc 12.0 the per-SM IMAD, SHF, LOP3 and IADD3 rates are 64, the same as 8.9 (BPG 13.4 Table 5). An NVIDIA employee on the throughput-table team says IMAD, LOP3 and IADD3 did not improve on Blackwell. Verifiers CONFIRMED this. The 128 'INT32 lanes' do not double IMAD. Possible upside (estimate): about 28% of the sm_120 hot-loop instructions are 2-operand IADD/ISETP, which do run 2x on 12.0. That suggests 1.0-1.15x per SM-clock. A forum IMAD-stream test at real clocks measured 1.43x against an overclocked 4090. Plausible range about 1.15-1.45.

gpus.gpu: B300 (HGX B300 SXM6 AC/PC, Blackwell Ultra) - the vast.ai listing
gpus.basis: VERIFIER-CORRECTED. 148 enabled SMs (several device reports; NVIDIA says only 'up to 160... varies by SKU') x 2.032 GHz (nvidia-smi max; it held 2032 MHz through a CUDA-core SGEMM at 875-976 W, under the 1100 W limit) = 300.7 SM-GHz. The researcher's 0.932 compares against the 4090's rated 2.52 GHz, so it is an upper bound. Both verifiers corrected it: real 4090s run about 2.68-2.75 GHz, giving 0.82-0.93, central 300.7 / 347.5 = 0.865 (about 0.87). cc 10.3 per-SM integer rates are identical to 8.9 (BPG 13.4). Blackwell Ultra's changes (FP64 cut, INT8 tensor cut, NVFP4 +50%, 288 GB HBM) do nothing for INT32, and float-to-int32 conversion drops to 2/clk on SM > 10.0. The 2^72 job is about 1.10-1.26 B300-years. VRAM is 288 GB = 275,040 MiB = 268.6 GiB, which is vast.ai's '269 GB'. L2 NOT FOUND.
